tickets.outcome_summary: Tauhid Zaman's size-S CC-TEE-WHITE tee was out of stock (0 on hand). Invoice 501 ($840, owed to Bulldog Print Co) was blocking that vendor from shipping a reprint; a human approved and paid it, which unblocked the vendor. The tee itself is still physically out of stock — no tool in this system can confirm a vendor shipment's arrival — so the ticket was resolved on the honest basis that the team's own work (clearing the invoice, giving the customer an accurate status) is complete, while the vendor's independent restock/ship timeline (5 days) is noted but not promised.

agent_contributions.contribution: Pulled the ticket, delegated to Inventory, Accounting, and Customer Service, then finalized the ticket as resolved once all three confirmed there was nothing further the team itself could do.
Confirmed CC-TEE-WHITE size S is still at 0 on hand (shortfall of 1) and identified Bulldog Print Co (apparel reprint, 5-day lead time) as the matching vendor.
Confirmed invoice 501 is paid ($840) and no longer blocks vendor shipping; confirmed no further payment or approval is needed.
Drafted (not sent) an honest customer-facing note explaining the tee is out of stock, the blocking invoice is now paid, and the vendor's 5-day lead time is an estimate, not a delivery promise.

human_approvals.result: Paid. Invoice 501 status flipped to paid; checking balance 3400.00 -> 2560.00.

tickets.outcome_summary: Chapel Street shop rent ($2,400, due 2026-09-02) was confirmed affordable and a human approved and paid it in full. On a later re-check, Accounting/Facilities correctly recognized (via the lease's own real payment history, not a guess) that this rent was already paid, rather than mistakenly treating the now-lower cash balance as a new shortfall.

agent_contributions.contribution: Pulled the ticket, delegated to Facilities and Accounting, then finalized the ticket as resolved once both confirmed the rent payment was already on record.
Verified lease 1's rent ($2,400, due 2026-09-02) and, on the final check, confirmed a real recorded payment already covers it.
Cross-checked the live cash balance against the lease's payment history and confirmed rent is paid, so no further payment or approval is needed.

tickets.outcome_summary: The Yale AI Club asked for 20 CC-HOOD-NAVY hoodies (size M) at a bulk discount, but only 8 were in stock (12 short). Accounting recommended a 10% discount ($52.20/unit, $30.20 margin/unit) as an affordable, specific option. A human reviewed that recommendation and approved the discount only for the 8 units actually in stock, explicitly declining to promise the unconfirmed remaining 12. The team then drafted an honest customer response reflecting exactly that scope.

agent_contributions.contribution: Pulled the ticket, delegated to Inventory and Accounting for the initial assessment, then (after the human's decision was recorded) delegated to Customer Service to finalize and marked the ticket resolved.
Confirmed 8 CC-HOOD-NAVY hoodies (size M) on hand against 20 requested (shortfall of 12) and identified Bulldog Print Co's 5-day lead time, without promising the shortfall.
Computed the real margin ($36/unit at list, $30.20/unit at a 10% discount) and recommended a specific 10% discount for human review, explicitly not approving it itself.
Drafted (not sent) a response to the Yale AI Club offering exactly the 8 in-stock hoodies at the approved $52.20 price, explicitly not promising the other 12.

human_approvals.result: Approved a 10% discount ($52.20/unit) on the 8 in-stock hoodies only; no payment tool involved — a price override has no execution tool, so the human's decision was recorded directly on the ticket (the same kind of direct, human-only control-plane action as approving a payment).
